newsitem.title: USA: Stocks extend bounce; money managers buy.
newsitem.headline: Stocks extend bounce; money managers buy.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose in erratic trading Wednesday, shrugging off profit-taking as bargain hunters and money managers continued to chase the market higher.
Just after 1:30 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 16.29 points at 7,774.35, adding to Tuesday's recovery of 154 points after Monday's 192-point plunge.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a narrow margin on volume of 330 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 3.84 points at 1,456.27.
The 30-share Dow index swung erratically, initially losing nearly 50 points before changing course and rising more than 50 points in late morning trading.

"This market is being driven by optimism and is obviously very strong," said Peggy Farley, chief executive officer of Amas Securities Inc. "Most issues are either up or down a little bit, which indicates strength."
Stocks got jostled as money managers adjusted their portfolios ahead of the end of the quarter, analysts said.

"There are two forces at work in this market," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "The positive force is that portfolio managers are trying to buy their favourite stocks at the quarter-end. But on the negative side, the bond market looks tired."

The day's first piece of economic news -- durable goods orders for May -- was mixed. It showed a drop of 0.6 percent while Wall Street analysts had expected an increase. But the drop was due partly to lower aircraft orders, which can swing widely from month to month.

"This only reinforces the argument that the Federal Reserve will keep monetary policy steady" at the July 1-2 meeting of policy-makers, said John Lonski, chief economist at Moody's Investors Service Inc.

While the durable goods report buoyed stocks, bonds got thrown off course by a jump in existing home sales. The National Association of Realtors said existing home sales rose 4.4 percent in May to a 4.24 million annual rate, well above Wall Street economists' forecasts for a 4.07 million rate.
The 30-year Treasury fell 6/32, or $1.88 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.71 percent from 6.69 percent Tuesday. The price and yield move in opposite directions.
Investors were also looking forward to good corporate earnings.
"The feeling is that the second quarter is going to be pretty good and that all of the bad news has already been pre-announced," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.

Among individual stocks, Liposome sank 15-9/16 to 9-1/4 after the company said the Phase III study of its Ventus drug to treat acute respiratory distress syndrome showed no difference between patients receiving the drug or a placebo.
Boston Chicken Inc. said weak sales and fewer new store openings would hurt earnings for 1997 and 1998. Its stock still managed to gain 5/16 to 15-3/4.
The American Stock Exchange index added 0.95 of a point to 620.81.
